Robot will read the notifications of the apps you tick here, keep their messages in memory only while their notifications are there, and read, summarize, translate or answer them when you ask. Nothing is written to storage, and nothing leaves the phone unless you send it. A message can never make Robot do anything: after one is read, every action asks first.

Robot reads the shade, not a database: no SMS permission, no message history. A message's text stays in memory until its notification goes; History keeps a line such as “Robot read 2 messages from Mom”, never the words, and the voice log keeps numbers only.

Replies go to the conversation the notification belongs to, never to anyone else, and only after you tap Send on the card (or, for someone you chose in People, after a 3-second stop). A sent message can't be recalled. An SMS reply may cost what your carrier charges. Some messaging apps mark the chat read and may send a read receipt when you reply from their notification. Some send an emoji alone as a reaction, and their Mark as read tells the sender.

Some apps show other apps only “New message” unless their notification settings show the name and message. Android hides messages that look like login codes from apps like Robot.
